title: The Buddy Ticket Programme Carried on a Granite Ridge Season Pass
content:
Each tier of the Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme loads a buddy lift ticket allotment onto the pass at activation, and the holder buys those tickets at the tier's buddy price for guests skiing with them.

**How a ticket is drawn.** A buddy ticket is drawn from the allotment on the day it is bought and is valid on that date at the mountain named on it; it is not dated forward and it is not refundable once the guest has been admitted on it.

**Blackout dates.** The tier's blackout dates apply to buddy tickets exactly as they apply to the pass itself, so a tier closed on a date cannot buy a buddy ticket for that date either.

**Once the allotment is used.** Further guest tickets are sold at the window price less the tier's friends and family reduction, and that reduction is taken instead of the buddy price rather than on top of it.

**Whose allotment it is.** The allotment belongs to the pass and not to the household, so allotments on two passes in one household are not pooled and an unused allotment does not pass to another pass or another season.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A Granite Ridge Local Pass carries an allotment of 4 buddy tickets at 119.00 each and a friends and family reduction of 15 per cent.

The holder brings a guest on four separate dates and pays 119.00 each time, drawing the allotment down to nothing. On a fifth date the guest is sold a window ticket at a hypothetical window price of 189.00 less 15 per cent, which is 160.65. The buddy price of 119.00 does not enter that figure, because the friends and family reduction is taken instead of the buddy price.

A second Granite Ridge Local Pass on the same household account carries its own allotment of 4. The first holder's exhausted allotment does not draw on it, and the second holder's unused tickets do not move across.
